decisions: SPINE: consent-safety proposal adopted as the base (unanimous judge winner); every fatal-flagged element replaced per the grafts below.

Org roles: FOUR values in CHECK — 'owner','admin','pharmacist','staff' — matching BACKLOG's literal 'owner/admin, pharmacist, staff'; owner+admin form the management tier with identical powers except owner-role management (only owners promote to / demote / deactivate owners); avoids a SQLite CHECK table-rebuild if admin were added later.

Owner succession: set_role promotion action (owner-only for the 'owner' value) so a second owner can exist — fixes the winner's impossible test 19 / permanent-single-owner dead end flagged fatal by judge 1.
users.role stays exactly 'patient'|'clinician'; org roles live only in organization_members (hard constraint 1); patients are refused membership at every entry point (org create, invite redeem).
One ACTIVE org membership per user, enforced by partial unique index ux_org_members_single_active — races fail closed at the DB; relaxing later = drop one index (membership is already a join table).

Client NEVER supplies organization_id anywhere: all org routes are singletons deriving the org from the caller's active membership; care-links/invitations POST accept only as_org:true + location_id (minimal-diff graft, adopted by all judges).
Membership is looked up per request inside resolveProfileAccess and route handlers, never cached in SessionUser — deactivation bites on the very next read.

Lazy-expiry stays INLINE in auth.ts as a candidate-loop 'continue' (no sweepExpiry import — access.ts line 11 already imports generateShareCode from auth.ts; importing back creates the cycle judge 1 flagged fatal). New src/lib/org.ts is a leaf module (imports only node:sqlite types).
Expired individual grant must NOT block a live org grant (and vice versa): the current early-return at auth.ts lines 150-156 becomes continue-to-next-candidate, with a dedicated regression test.

Index migration: DROP INDEX ux_grants_open + the two replacement partial uniques live in migrateColumns AFTER defensive try/catch ALTERs, and the old ux_grants_open CREATE lines (db.ts 151-152) are DELETED from SCHEMA — SCHEMA runs first every boot and would otherwise recreate the dropped index forever (judge 1 fatal; minimal-diff graft).

Defensive try/catch ALTERs for organization_id on access_grants and patient_invitations are included even though current SCHEMA has them — no-op insurance for any pre-Phase-6 database file, per repo convention (columns appear in both SCHEMA CREATE and migrateColumns, like actual_use/provenance).

Existing individual grants (organization_id NULL) are never rewritten, never matched by the org branch, and never visible to any org — org access exists only via a NEW patient-approved grant naming the org (hard constraint 4).

Location is consent CONTEXT, not an enforcement boundary: members are not location-assigned, so consent copy says explicitly that approval covers everyone at the organization including other locations and future staff — honest disclosure over false implied scoping (all three proposals converged).

Alert-reviews route redesigned against the REAL code (it never calls resolveProfileAccess — inline grant SELECT at lines 37-44, profile derived from the alert row): the inline query gains the org-membership branch, closing the fail-open where a deactivated requester could still write reviews against a live org grant (judge-flagged as the most consequential defect).

Reviews under org access require org_role IN ('owner','pharmacist'); 'admin' and 'staff' get 403 — reviews are clinical judgments, the management tier is not the clinical tier; owner included because pharmacist-owners are the norm.

Review attribution: reviewer_clinic snapshots the ORGANIZATION name at write time when authored under org access (the column is already snapshot-semantic); review_created audit meta gains { via:'org', org }.

Review withdrawal (DELETE /api/alert-reviews/[id]) stays author-only and grant-check-free as today: withdrawal re-surfaces the alert (fail-safe direction) and org colleagues already correct via supersede-by-new-review; resolves the judges' un-designed DELETE question.

record_opened stays logged at the single existing point (medications GET) — the clinic record page always fetches medications, so it is one event per open; logging alerts/exposure GETs too would triple-count each view; the meta now carries {via, org, grant} for attribution.

Org-scoped patient invitations whose MINTER is no longer an active member fail CLOSED: invitation lazily flips to 'cancelled' (audit meta reason:'minter_inactive') and intake 410s — replaces the winner's conclude-normally stance (all three judges grafted this).

Staff invites are ALSO minter-staleness-checked lazily at view/redeem: an invite minted by a since-deactivated owner/admin flips to 'cancelled' — minted authority dies with revoked authority, closing the fired-manager pocket-invite hole; deactivation response still returns open_invite_count so owners review invites minted by others.

No reactivate flow: rejoining after deactivation requires a fresh invite (new membership row; the partial unique index only constrains ACTIVE rows). Self-deactivation is allowed except for the last active owner — leaving is legitimate; the last-owner guard covers lockout.
Staff invites mint 'admin'/'pharmacist'/'staff' only, never 'owner' (creation or promotion only); role is fixed at mint time and read from the invite row, never the request body.
Request-form default is 'Myself' (individual) — the conservative consent default while orgs are unverified; org scope is an explicit selection (judge 3's concern; minimal-diff's stance).

Upgrade path INCLUDED: a member holding an ACTIVE individual grant may mint a PENDING org request without re-reading the care code; justification: the patient already consented to this person individually, only a PENDING row is created, and the patient still explicitly approves the org card — no silent widening (2 of 3 judges grafted it).
Pending org requests are visible only to the requester plus owners/admins — pharmacist/staff members never see patient names the patient has not yet approved for the org (unanimous graft).

Roster dedupe: one row per profile with access_via badges; org-ACTIVE grant relinquishment is management-tier only, PENDING withdrawal is requester-or-management; UI copy states the other door survives in both directions.
Patient revocation of an org grant uses the existing endpoint unchanged — one click flips the single grant row and every member 403s on their next read.

Two-door visibility: /api/access computes an overlap flag per active grant (individual grant whose clinician is an active member of an org that also holds a grant, and vice versa) and AccessPanel renders 'revoking this does not remove that' on both cards — addresses judge 2's highest-stakes UX unresolved with one EXISTS subquery.

Closed locations are refused for NEW requests/invitations; existing grants keep their stored location_id and render with a '(location closed)' suffix; no notification event — access semantics never depended on location, so there is no consent change to notify about.

'Unverified' labeling: organizations.verification_status ('unverified' only — no route can set 'verified') badged on every patient-facing and join surface; individual professional accounts get a static shared footnote on all consent cards + clinic header ('GanderMed has not verified this professional's or organization's credentials') — no users column because no verification process exists, so a column would fabricate a distinction.

The reviews-route org check is the ONE org authorization decision outside resolveProfileAccess; it gets a CLAUDE.md hard-rule note plus dedicated tests so future write-ish features (Phase 10 dispositions) replicate it.

In passing, the reviews route's expiry comparison switches from SQL datetime('now') (space-separated format, lexically incomparable with stored ISO 'T' strings — same-day expiries slip through today) to a JS ISO parameter — one-line honesty fix, noted in the commit.

Audit: every org lifecycle event and org-scoped open lands in audit_events as ids + enum strings only (PHI-free, hard constraint 6); org-admin events carry profile_id NULL so they never leak into patient feeds via the existing profile filter.

TS gotcha (constraint 7): explicit union return annotations on resolveProfileAccess, activeMembership, requireOrgMember/requireOrgManagement, redeemStaffInvite, and every new multi-literal helper, following the documented requireClinician pattern in src/app/api/invitations/route.ts.
blueprint.ddl:
-- ================= 1. APPEND to the SCHEMA constant in src/lib/db.ts =================
-- (order matters inside the string: organizations before organization_locations)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS organizations (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  verification_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unverified'
    CHECK (verification_status IN ('unverified','verified')),
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS organization_locations (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,
  address TEXT,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','closed')),
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_org_locations_org ON organization_locations(organization_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS organization_members (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  org_role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (org_role IN ('owner','admin','pharmacist','staff')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','deactivated')),
  invited_by_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  deactivated_at TEXT,
  deactivated_by_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_org_members_org ON organization_members(organization_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_org_members_user ON organization_members(user_id);
-- One ACTIVE org per user (Phase 5 decision); deactivated history rows coexist.
-- Relaxing to multi-org later = drop this one index.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_org_members_single_active
  ON organization_members(user_id) WHERE status = 'active';

-- Same hashed-token pattern as patient_invitations: sha256 stored, raw token
-- shown exactly once in the mint response, lazy expiry at read time.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS staff_invitations (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  invited_by_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  org_role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (org_role IN ('admin','pharmacist','staff')),  -- 'owner' is never minted
  invitee_label TEXT,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'created' CHECK (status IN ('created','redeemed','expired','cancelled')),
  expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  redeemed_at TEXT,
  redeemed_by_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),
  cancelled_at TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_staff_invites_org ON staff_invitations(organization_id, created_at);

-- ================= 2. EDIT existing SCHEMA lines =================
-- access_grants CREATE TABLE: add   location_id INTEGER,   after organization_id
--   (bare INTEGER, matching the existing organization_id style on this table).
-- patient_invitations CREATE TABLE: add   location_id INTEGER,   after organization_id.
-- DELETE lines 151-152 (the ux_grants_open CREATE UNIQUE INDEX) from SCHEMA entirely —
--   migrateColumns owns the grant-uniqueness index family from now on. Leaving it
--   would recreate the dropped index on every boot (SCHEMA runs before migrateColumns).

-- ================= 3. APPEND to migrateColumns() in src/lib/db.ts =================
-- Each ALTER in its own try/catch {} ("column already exists"), exactly the existing pattern:
ALTER TABLE access_grants ADD COLUMN organization_id INTEGER;        -- defensive no-op on current DBs
ALTER TABLE access_grants ADD COLUMN location_id INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE patient_invitations ADD COLUMN organization_id INTEGER;  -- defensive no-op on current DBs
ALTER TABLE patient_invitations ADD COLUMN location_id INTEGER;

-- Then, OUTSIDE try/catch (all idempotent; must run AFTER the ALTERs above so the
-- partial-index WHERE clauses can reference organization_id on any vintage of DB):
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_grants_open;
-- Split uniqueness: one open INDIVIDUAL grant per (profile, clinician); one open ORG
-- grant per (profile, organization) across ALL requesters. All pre-Phase-5 rows have
-- organization_id NULL and land under the individual index with identical semantics.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_grants_open_individual
  ON access_grants(profile_id, clinician_user_id)
  WHERE status IN ('pending','active') AND organization_id IS NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_grants_open_org
  ON access_grants(profile_id, organization_id)
  WHERE status IN ('pending','active') AND organization_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_grants_org
  ON access_grants(organization_id) WHERE organization_id IS NOT NULL;

-- No data backfill of any kind: existing grants keep organization_id NULL forever.
-- Reminder (CLAUDE.md): restart the dev server after this lands — the DB singleton
-- on globalThis survives hot reload, so getDb() must run fresh.
blueprint.authorization:
NEW LEAF MODULE src/lib/org.ts (imports only node:sqlite types — cycle-free; auth.ts, access.ts, and routes import from it):
- export function activeMembership(db: DatabaseSync, userId: number): { member_id: number; organization_id: number; org_role: "owner" | "admin" | "pharmacist" | "staff" } | null — SELECT id, organization_id, org_role FROM organization_members WHERE user_id = ? AND status = 'active' (at most one row via ux_org_members_single_active). Explicit union annotation (repo TS gotcha).
- export const isManagement = (r) => r === "owner" || r === "admin";  export const canReview = (r) => r === "owner" || r === "pharmacist".
- Route helpers requireOrgMember(request) / requireOrgManagement(request), modeled on requireClinician in src/app/api/invitations/route.ts, returning { fail: NextResponse } | { db; user; membership; org } with the explicit union annotation.

resolveProfileAccess (src/lib/auth.ts) — patient and write branches byte-identical; return type becomes an explicit union:
  export function resolveProfileAccess(db, user, request, opts: { write: boolean }):
    | { profileId: number; via: "self" | "individual" | "org"; grantId: number | null; organizationId: number | null }
    | { error: string; status: number }
All existing call sites keep compiling: they discriminate on '"error" in access' and read only profileId; the success arm only gains fields. Clinician-read logic, in order (every branch fails closed):
1. patient -> { profileId, via: "self", grantId: null, organizationId: null } (500 if profile missing — unchanged).
2. opts.write -> 403 view-only BEFORE any lookup (org roles never unlock writes — hard constraint 5 holds structurally).
3. Parse ?patient=<id> (unchanged 400).
4. const m = activeMembership(db, user.id)  // null when never joined OR deactivated — checked per request, never cached.
5. Candidates, individual first for audit attribution:
   SELECT id, status, expires_at, profile_id, organization_id, location_id FROM access_grants
   WHERE profile_id = ? AND status = 'active'
     AND ((organization_id IS NULL AND clinician_user_id = ?)
       OR (organization_id IS NOT NULL AND organization_id = ?))
   ORDER BY organization_id IS NULL DESC, id
   bound as (profileId, user.id, m?.organization_id ?? -1). The -1 sentinel means no membership matches nothing — a deactivated or never-member clinician can never ride an org grant, even for an org they used to belong to.
6. For EACH candidate, the existing inline lazy-expiry block (UPDATE ... WHERE status='active' + raw INSERT of the access_expired audit row with actor NULL, targetId = grant id) — but the current early-return at lines 150-156 becomes `continue`: an expired individual grant must not block a live org grant, and vice versa. First surviving candidate returns { profileId, via: g.organization_id == null ? "individual" : "org", grantId: g.id, organizationId: g.organization_id }.
7. No survivor -> existing 403 "No active patient-approved access for this record."
Audit at the read site: medications GET (the single record_opened log point — kept single because the clinic record page always fetches medications once per open; logging alerts/exposure GETs would triple-count) passes meta from the access result: via "org" -> { via: "org", org: organizationId, grant: grantId }; via "individual" -> { via: "individual", grant: grantId }. Ids and enums only — PHI-free.

sweepExpiry (access.ts): unchanged — org grants ride the identical status machine wherever grants are LISTED (roster GET, /api/access GET).
revokeGrant (access.ts): scope type widens to { patientProfileId?; clinicianUserId?; organizationId? }; organizationId requires grant.organization_id === scope.organizationId (route verifies caller's management membership first). Patient revocation is UNCHANGED — patientProfileId already matches org grants, so one patient click cuts off the entire org on every member's next read. Audit meta.by becomes "patient" | "clinician" | "organization".
decideGrant: mechanically unchanged (org/location were fixed at request time; approval flips pending->active); it now reads the grant row it already fetched and adds meta { scope: "organization", org, location } to access_approved when organization_id is set.
Membership deactivation NEVER mutates grants — the org grant belongs to the patient↔organization relationship; only the live membership check gates who exercises it. The deactivated member's own individual grants are personal consents the org has no authority over.

ALERT REVIEWS — designed against the REAL route (src/app/api/alert-reviews/route.ts does NOT call resolveProfileAccess; it has an inline access_grants SELECT at lines 37-44 keyed on clinician_user_id, takes alert_id in the body, derives profile from the alert row). POST changes:
- Replace the inline SELECT with the org-aware equivalent (same shape as the resolveProfileAccess candidate query, filter-style expiry with a JS ISO `now` parameter — fixing in passing the current datetime('now')-vs-ISO lexical mismatch):
  SELECT id, organization_id FROM access_grants
  WHERE profile_id = ? AND status = 'active' AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?)
    AND ((organization_id IS NULL AND clinician_user_id = ?)
      OR (organization_id IS NOT NULL AND organization_id = ?))
  ORDER BY organization_id IS NULL DESC LIMIT 1
  bound (alert.profile_id, nowISO, user.id, activeMembership(db, user.id)?.organization_id ?? -1).
- No grant -> 403 (this is what closes the fail-open: a deactivated requester's membership lookup returns null, the sentinel matches nothing, and only their nonexistent individual grant could authorize).
- Grant is org-scoped AND !canReview(membership.org_role) -> 403 "Alert reviews require a pharmacist or owner account in your organization." ('admin' and 'staff' blocked — clinical tier, not management tier.)
- reviewer_clinic snapshots the ORG name (SELECT name FROM organizations) when authored under org access, else user.clinic_name as today; review_created audit meta gains { via: "org", org } when org-authored.
DELETE /api/alert-reviews/[id]: unchanged (author-only via reviewer_user_id, no grant check) — withdrawal re-surfaces the alert (fail-safe) and colleagues correct via the existing supersede-by-new-review semantics.
This reviews check is the ONE org authorization decision outside resolveProfileAccess — documented as a hard-rule note in CLAUDE.md and pinned by tests 25-26.
blueprint.request_consent_flow:
CARE-CODE PATH. POST /api/care-links body becomes { code, purpose, as_org?: boolean, location_id?: number } (never an organization_id — the org is derived server-side). Absent as_org -> today's individual request, byte-for-byte. With as_org: the route loads activeMembership (403 "You are not an active member of an organization" if null — any org_role may request, the patient is the gate), validates location_id references an ACTIVE location of THAT org (400 otherwise; a location is required for org requests), then calls requestAccessByCode(db, user.id, code, purpose, org: { organizationId, locationId } | null). Inside requestAccessByCode the duplicate check becomes scope-aware: individual requests collide on (profile, clinician, organization_id IS NULL) as today; org requests collide on (profile_id, organization_id) ACROSS ALL requesters — 409 "Your organization already has a pending or active request for this patient" (ux_grants_open_org is the DB backstop). The INSERT stores organization_id + location_id, with clinician_user_id = requested_by_user_id = the requesting member (provenance only — never an access key on org grants). Audit access_requested meta { as: "organization", org, location } (ids only).

UPGRADE PATH (adoption story for existing solo clinicians — consent-gated, no silent widening): POST /api/care-links with { upgrade_profile_id, location_id, purpose? } and no code. Allowed only when the caller holds an ACTIVE unexpired INDIVIDUAL grant for that profile AND an active membership (else 404/403, nothing created). Creates a normal PENDING org grant (same 409-on-duplicate rule); the patient still explicitly approves the org card; the individual grant is untouched either way. Audit meta adds via: "upgrade". Clinic roster shows a "Request team access" button on individual-only rows.

WHAT THE PATIENT SEES (AccessPanel). /api/access GET adds LEFT JOINs to organizations and organization_locations and returns per grant: organization_name, org_verification_status, location_label, location_status, requested_by_name, requested_by_active (whether the requester's membership is still active), and overlap (EXISTS-subquery: for an org grant, an active individual grant on this profile whose clinician is an active member of this org; symmetric for individual grants). A pending ORG request card is visually distinct and shows: the org name with an always-on "Unverified organization" badge, the location ("Wortley Village — 123 Main St" and "(location closed)" if since closed), "requested by <member>", purpose, date, and the load-bearing disclosure verbatim: "Approving shares your record, view-only, with everyone at <Org name> — including staff at other locations and staff who join later. You can revoke at any time." Same Approve/Deny buttons and 30/90/180-day expiry select — decideGrant needs no mechanical change. Individual pending cards are pixel-identical to today plus the shared unverified-professional footnote. There is NO path that converts an individual grant into an org grant: an org needing access to an already-individually-linked patient sends a NEW org request (code or upgrade path) and gets a NEW approval; both grants then coexist under the split unique indexes, and the overlap flag makes the two doors visible to the patient on both cards ("Dr. X also has separate personal access — revoking this does not remove that").

The clinic request form gains a "Request as" selector rendered only when GET /api/auth/me shows a membership: default "Myself — <display name>" (conservative default while orgs are unverified), then one option per ACTIVE location: "<Org name> — <location label>".
blueprint.staff_invites:
Implementation lives in src/lib/org.ts, cloning the invitations.ts pattern (sha256 token hash stored, raw token shown once, lazy expiry, explicit union return on the redeem helper: "ok" | "not_found" | "gone" | "patient" | "already_member" | "other_org").

MINT — POST /api/org/invites, management tier only (owner/admin via requireOrgManagement; pharmacist/staff 403, non-members 403, patients 403, anonymous 401). Body { org_role: "admin" | "pharmacist" | "staff", invitee_label?: string (<=80 chars, owner-side display only), expires_days?: 1..14 default 7 }. 'owner' is never mintable (CHECK-enforced) — ownership arises from org creation or set_role promotion. Server generates randomBytes(32).toString("base64url"), stores only the sha256 hex, responds once with join_path "/join-org/<token>"; the list endpoint never returns raw tokens. Rate-limited via src/lib/ratelimit.ts. Audit org_staff_invite_created meta { org, role, expires_days }. Handover is out-of-band by design (hard constraint 2): shown/printed/QR, exactly like patient invitations.

VIEW — GET /api/org/join/[token], public. Resolves by hash; applies TWO lazy sweeps in order: (1) past expires_at while 'created' -> flip 'expired' (audit org_staff_invite_expired, actor NULL); (2) minter no longer an active owner/admin of the org -> flip 'cancelled' (audit org_staff_invite_cancelled meta { reason: "minter_inactive" }) — minted authority dies with revoked authority, closing the fired-manager pocket-invite hole. Returns only { org_name, verification_status, org_role, invited_by_name, status, viewer: "anonymous" | "patient" | "clinician" | "member" } — no member list, no patient data; unknown/tampered token -> 404 with no detail.

REDEEM — POST /api/org/join/[token], decision table in order:
- unknown token -> 404; status expired/cancelled/redeemed after sweeps -> 410 (one-time redemption; replay refused).
- no session -> 401; the /join-org page links /login and /register with ?next=/join-org/<token> so the token survives the auth round-trip.
- user.role === 'patient' -> 403 "Patient accounts cannot join a care organization." Invite stays 'created' (still usable by the right person); users.role and organization_members untouched (hard constraints 1 and 5).
- already an ACTIVE member of THIS org -> 409 "You are already a member."; invite stays 'created'.
- ACTIVE member of ANOTHER org -> 409 "This account already belongs to <other org>. One organization per account in this version."; invite stays 'created' (no silent moves).
- success: one transaction — INSERT organization_members (organization_id, user_id, org_role FROM THE INVITE ROW (request body ignored), status 'active', invited_by_user_id) + UPDATE staff_invitations SET status='redeemed', redeemed_at, redeemed_by_user_id WHERE id = ? AND status = 'created' (double-submit guard; first wins on the synchronous connection). A ux_org_members_single_active constraint violation is caught -> 409 (races fail closed). Audit org_member_joined meta { org, role, invite }.

CANCEL — POST /api/org/invites/[id] { action: "cancel" }, management tier of the owning org; anyone else 404 (existence not revealed, matching invitations convention); only from 'created'; audit org_staff_invite_cancelled. Redeem after cancel -> 410.

MEMBER MANAGEMENT — POST /api/org/members/[id]:
- { action: "deactivate" }: management tier; target must be an active member of the caller's org (404). Deactivating an OWNER requires the caller to be an owner (admins 403), and the LAST active owner can never be deactivated (409 "Promote another owner first") — including self. Non-last-owner self-deactivation is allowed (leaving is legitimate). Sets status='deactivated', deactivated_at, deactivated_by_user_id. Enforcement is immediate: resolveProfileAccess re-reads membership per request, so the ex-member's next org read 403s, their roster loses every org patient, their org-scoped patient invitations and their minted staff invites die lazily, and their own individual grants are untouched (personal consents the org has no authority over). Response includes open_invite_count (org invites still 'created', i.e. minted by others) and the UI prompts the owner to review/cancel them. Audit org_member_deactivated meta { org, member_user }.
- { action: "set_role", org_role }: promotion/demotion. Setting to or from 'owner' requires the caller to be an owner; other transitions require management tier; demoting the last active owner -> 409. This is the succession mechanism (fixes the judged-fatal impossible-second-owner dead end). Audit org_member_role_changed meta { org, member_user, role }.
- NO reactivate action: rejoining requires a fresh invite (new membership row; the partial unique index only constrains ACTIVE rows, so history is preserved).

ORG BOOTSTRAP — POST /api/org: clinician with NO active membership (member -> 409, patient -> 403). Body { name, location_label, location_address? } — an org is born with one location so org requests can always name one. One transaction: organizations row (verification_status 'unverified'; no code path can ever set 'verified') + first location + creator's 'owner' membership. Audit org_created + org_location_added + org_member_joined meta { via: "created", role: "owner" }.
blueprint.roster_and_revocation:
ROSTER (GET /api/care-links, clinician). Grant query widens to: status IN ('pending','active') AND ((clinician_user_id = :me AND organization_id IS NULL) OR (organization_id = :myOrg)) with :myOrg = activeMembership(me)?.organization_id ?? -1 (no membership -> org half matches nothing). Each row swept with sweepExpiry exactly as today. ACTIVE grants are then GROUPED BY profile_id: one roster row per patient regardless of how many grants reach them; stats (recomputeAlerts + attachReviews, open-alert counts excluding reviewed/acknowledged, med count, last dose) computed ONCE per profile. Each entry keeps today's fields and adds access: [{ grant_id, via: "individual" | "org", purpose, expires_at, location_label?, requested_by_name?, requested_by_active? }] plus a via summary for badges — "you", "via <Org> · <location>", or both. Org rows render "requested by <member>" with "(no longer at this pharmacy)" when requested_by_active is false. PENDING section: the caller's own individual pendings (as today) PLUS the org's pendings visible ONLY to the requester and owners/admins — pharmacist/staff never see patient names the patient hasn't approved for the org (pre-consent name-exposure minimization). Every active member including 'staff' sees the ACTIVE org roster (that is the disclosed meaning of the org grant); no member ever sees another member's individual-only patients.

CLINICIAN-SIDE REMOVE (DELETE /api/care-links/[id]): individual grants — unchanged, self only (revokeGrant clinicianUserId scope). Org PENDING requests — withdrawable by the requester or any owner/admin. Org ACTIVE grants — management tier ONLY (it destroys access for the whole org): route checks membership + isManagement then calls revokeGrant(db, user.id, id, { organizationId }); requester-non-management sees no control and the API 403s regardless. Confirm dialog: "Give up <Org>'s access to <patient>? Everyone at the organization loses it; the patient would have to approve a new request." When a clinician removes their INDIVIDUAL grant on a deduped row, the UI states "You will still see this patient through <Org> until the patient or an owner/admin removes that access" — no silent surprises in either direction. Audit access_revoked meta { by: "organization" }.

PATIENT SIDE (AccessPanel). An active org grant renders as the ORGANIZATION's access, deliberately not the requester's: "<Org name> — <location label>" with "Pharmacy team access" and "Unverified organization" chips, secondary line "Everyone at this organization can view your record · requested by <member> · since <date> · expires <date>/no expiry". Revoke uses the EXISTING button and endpoint (POST /api/access/[id] { action: "revoke" } -> revokeGrant patientProfileId scope, which already matches org grants) with org-specific confirm copy: "Revoke access for <Org name>? Everyone at this organization immediately loses the ability to view your record." The single row flips to 'revoked' and every member — including the original requester — 403s on their very next read via resolveProfileAccess. Revoking an org grant never touches a separately-approved individual grant and vice versa; the overlap flag renders the two-door note on both cards, and after a revoke the panel surfaces "Dr. X still has separate personal access below" when applicable. Expiry chosen at approval applies to the whole org (it is one grant); lazy expiry writes the same access_expired audit row. Past org grants appear in the existing past-requests list under the org name. The activity feed: /api/access's audit query additionally selects a.meta, the server resolves meta.org -> org name, and record_opened rows render "<Member name> viewed your record via <Org name> (unverified)".
api_routes: POST /api/org — clinician with NO active membership (member 409, patient 403) — create org + first location + owner membership in one transaction; rate-limited.

GET /api/org — any signed-in clinician — caller's org context: { organization: null } when member-less, else org (name, verification_status), my org_role, locations, members (name, role, status, joined); open staff invites included only for owner/admin; patients 403.
POST /api/org/locations — owner/admin — add a location; audit org_location_added.
POST /api/org/locations/[id] — owner/admin — { action: 'close' }: refused for new requests/invitations thereafter; existing grants keep the stored location_id for display.
POST /api/org/invites — owner/admin — mint staff invite (role admin|pharmacist|staff, 1-14d expiry); raw join token returned exactly once; rate-limited.
POST /api/org/invites/[id] — owner/admin of the owning org (others 404) — { action: 'cancel' } from 'created'.
GET /api/org/join/[token] — public — invite metadata (org name + unverified badge, offered role, inviter, status, viewer); lazy expiry + minter-staleness sweeps; unknown token 404.

POST /api/org/join/[token] — signed-in clinician — redeem per decision table (patient 403 no-consume, same-org 409 no-consume, other-org 409 no-consume, terminal 410, success = membership + 'redeemed' in one transaction); rate-limited.

POST /api/org/members/[id] — owner/admin (owner-only for owner-role targets and for set_role to/from 'owner'; last-active-owner guard) — { action: 'deactivate' } | { action: 'set_role', org_role }; deactivate response carries open_invite_count.

POST /api/care-links (EXTENDED) — clinician — body adds as_org + location_id (membership + active-location validated server-side; org never client-supplied) and the upgrade variant { upgrade_profile_id, location_id } gated on an ACTIVE individual grant; org duplicate 409 keyed on (profile, org).
GET /api/care-links (EXTENDED) — clinician — roster unions individual + my-org grants, dedupes per profile with access[] scopes; org pendings visible to requester + owner/admin only.
DELETE /api/care-links/[id] (EXTENDED) — clinician — individual: self only (unchanged); org pending: requester or owner/admin; org active: owner/admin only (revokeGrant organizationId scope).

GET /api/access (EXTENDED) — patient — grants gain organization_name, org_verification_status, location_label, location_status, requested_by_name, requested_by_active, overlap; audit query now selects meta and resolves org names for 'via <Org>' rendering.
POST /api/access/[id] (UNCHANGED) — patient — approve/deny/revoke works identically for org grants; access_approved audit gains org meta when applicable.
POST /api/invitations (EXTENDED) — clinician — body adds as_org + location_id with the same membership/location validation; stored on patient_invitations.

GET /api/intake/[token] (EXTENDED) — public — meta adds organization_name, org_verification_status, location_label when org-scoped; org invitations lazily flip to 'cancelled' (410) when the minter is no longer an active member.

POST /api/intake/[token]/consent (EXTENDED) — signed-in patient — org-aware concludeIntake: reuse keyed on (profile, org) for org invitations, (profile, clinician, organization_id IS NULL) for individual ones; approve writes an ACTIVE org grant carrying organization_id + location_id.

POST /api/alert-reviews (REWRITTEN CHECK) — clinician — inline grant check replaced with the org-aware candidate query + per-request membership; org-authored reviews require org_role owner|pharmacist ('admin'/'staff' 403); reviewer_clinic snapshots the org name; this closes the deactivated-requester fail-open.
DELETE /api/alert-reviews/[id] (UNCHANGED) — clinician — author-only withdrawal; colleagues correct via supersede-by-new-review.
GET /api/auth/me (EXTENDED) — any signed-in user — response adds org: { id, name, org_role, verification_status } | null, computed fresh per call (never cached in SessionUser).
GET /api/medications (EXTENDED META) — via resolveProfileAccess — record_opened audit row gains { via, org?, grant } from the access result; remains the single record-open log point.
All other profile-scoped reads (alerts, exposure, dose-events GET, chat) — UNCHANGED CODE — inherit org access automatically through resolveProfileAccess.

blueprint.phase6_wiring: POST /api/invitations accepts { as_org?: boolean, location_id?: number } with identical server-side validation to care-links (active membership required — any org_role may mint, consent still gates; location must be an ACTIVE location of the caller's org; the org id itself is always derived from membership, never from the body). createInvitation gains an org param and stores organization_id + location_id on patient_invitations (columns exist / added defensively); invitation_created audit meta gains { org, location }. GET /api/intake/[token] meta returns organization_name, org_verification_status, location_label so the patient sees the ORGANIZATION and its Unverified badge BEFORE starting intake; the consent step renders the same disclosure copy as AccessPanel and the approve button names the org. STALENESS (fail closed — unanimous judge graft replacing the spine's conclude-normally): the invitation-resolve helper used by all intake routes gains a lazy sweep alongside sweepInvitationExpiry — if invitation.organization_id is set and the minting clinician no longer holds an ACTIVE membership in that org, flip the invitation to 'cancelled' (audit invitation_cancelled meta { reason: 'minter_inactive' }) so meta/start/submit/consent all uniformly refuse via the existing terminal-status handling (410); a deactivated employee's outstanding links can never mint org access. concludeIntake branches on invitation.organization_id: when set, the open-grant reuse lookup keys on (profile_id, organization_id, status IN ('pending','active')) — reusing an active org grant or activating a pending org care-code request in place (mirrors the existing individual reuse test; exactly one row per (patient, org)) — else INSERTs an ACTIVE grant carrying organization_id + location_id + clinician_user_id = invitation.clinician_user_id (provenance) + approved_by/starts_at/expires_at as today. CRITICAL SAME-COMMIT FIX: the EXISTING individual reuse lookup at invitations.ts lines 178-182 must gain AND organization_id IS NULL — without it, an individual invitation's consent could grab and re-stamp a coexisting org grant row for the same (patient, clinician), silently corrupting scope (this is the concrete instance of the index-split hazard every proposal warned about; regression test 29 pins it). Denial still shares nothing and creates no grant; consent never touches, reuses, or widens an individual grant when concluding an org invitation, and vice versa.
test_plan: 1. Org create authz: patient POST /api/org -> 403; fresh clinician -> 200 creating org (verification_status 'unverified') + first location + 'owner' membership in one transaction; the same clinician again -> 409.

2. GET /api/org shape: member-less clinician -> 200 { organization: null }; member -> org + locations + members; the invites section appears for owner and admin but not pharmacist/staff; patient -> 403.

3. Staff invite mint authz + secrecy: pharmacist and staff POST /api/org/invites -> 403; admin and owner -> 200; DB row stores a 64-char sha256 hex not containing the raw token; no list endpoint ever returns a raw token (mirror of the Phase 6 SECRECY test).
4. Redeem happy path: fresh clinician POSTs /api/org/join/[token] -> 200; active membership carries the INVITE row's role; invite flips 'redeemed' with redeemed_by; replaying the same token -> 410.
5. Patient cannot redeem: patient session -> 403; invite REMAINS 'created' (assert unchanged); organization_members row count unchanged; users.role untouched.
6. Token lifecycle: anonymous redeem -> 401; tampered/unknown token -> 404; backdated expires_at -> GET meta shows 'expired' (row lazily flipped) and redeem -> 410; cancelled invite -> 410.
7. Role fixed at mint: a redeem request body claiming org_role 'owner' is ignored; membership gets the invite's minted role.

8. Single-org rule: active member of org B redeeming an org A invite -> 409, no membership row (partial unique index holds), invite stays 'created'; active member of org A redeeming an org A invite -> 409, invite stays 'created'.
9. Minter-stale staff invite: deactivate the admin who minted an open invite -> GET meta shows 'cancelled' (lazy flip, audit meta reason 'minter_inactive'); redeem -> 410.

10. set_role succession: owner promotes a pharmacist to 'owner' -> 200; an admin attempting set_role to 'owner' -> 403; demoting the last active owner -> 409; after promotion, deactivating the original owner succeeds (last-owner guard now passes) — the succession path is exercised through the API, not DB seeding.

11. Deactivation rules: admin deactivates a staff member -> 200 with open_invite_count in the response; admin deactivating an OWNER -> 403; sole owner self-deactivation -> 409; non-last-owner self-deactivation -> 200; deactivated member re-joins via a FRESH invite -> new active row inserted.

12. Org care-code request: member POSTs /api/care-links { code, as_org, location_id } -> pending grant row carries organization_id + location_id and requested_by = the member; non-member with as_org -> 403 and zero new grant rows; location belonging to another org, or a closed location -> 400 and zero rows.

13. Duplicate scoping: with an open org request for (P, org), a DIFFERENT member requesting P as-org -> 409 and exactly one open (P, org) row; the SAME clinician may hold an open individual grant AND the org an open org grant for P simultaneously (split partial indexes).

14. Org approval semantics: patient approves the org request with 90-day expiry -> grant active with organization_id, location_id, expires_at; the requester AND a different active member both GET /api/medications?patient=P -> 200; audit access_approved meta.scope='organization'; record_opened meta = { via:'org', org, grant } and contains no PHI.
15. Strangers blocked: a clinician with no membership -> 403 on an org-granted patient; an active member of org B -> 403 on an org-A-granted patient.

16. Deactivated member fails closed: after deactivation, that member's very next read -> 403 while the grant row is still 'active'; other members still 200; the deactivated member's own INDIVIDUAL grants on other patients still 200.

17. NEVER-WIDEN core (constraint 4): pre-existing individual grant (organization_id NULL) for clinician C; C creates/joins org O; every co-member of O -> 403 and their roster excludes the patient; C still reads 200 with record_opened meta.via='individual'; the grant row's organization_id is still NULL.

18. Expiry ordering regression: C holds a backdated-EXPIRED individual grant while C's org holds a LIVE org grant -> C reads 200 via org, the individual row flips 'expired' with an access_expired audit row (candidate loop continues instead of early-returning); symmetric case (org expired, individual live) also reads 200.
19. Org grant expiry: backdate expires_at -> any member's next read -> 403, row flips 'expired', access_expired audit written once (lazy sweep through resolveProfileAccess).

20. Independent doors on revocation: patient revokes the org grant -> EVERY member including the requester 403s next read, audit access_revoked; a separately-approved individual grant to a member keeps working; then revoking the individual grant blocks that clinician entirely.

21. Roster dedupe + staff visibility: clinician with both individual and org access to P -> exactly ONE roster row with both scopes in access[]; a staff-role member sees org-granted patients but NOT any member's individual-only patients.
22. Pending visibility: an org pending request appears in the roster response for the requester and for owner/admin members, and does NOT appear for a pharmacist/staff non-requester.

23. Clinician-side removal authz: individual grant DELETE by non-grantee -> 404 (unchanged); org PENDING withdrawable by requester or admin; org ACTIVE removal by pharmacist requester -> 403, by admin/owner -> 200 with audit meta.by='organization'; after org removal, members 403 but any individual grant survives.

24. Upgrade path: member with an ACTIVE individual grant POSTs { upgrade_profile_id, location_id } -> 200 pending org grant, record still closed to other members until the patient approves; without an active individual grant -> 404 and nothing created.

25. Reviews under org access (the fail-open fix): with only an org grant — staff POST /api/alert-reviews -> 403; admin -> 403; pharmacist -> 200 with reviewer_clinic = org name and review_created meta.org; owner -> 200; the ORIGINAL REQUESTER after being deactivated -> 403 (this is the exact fail-open judge 2 flagged); a review under a plain individual grant is unchanged.

26. Review withdrawal stays author-only: another org member DELETE on a colleague's review -> 404; the author -> 200; superseding via a new POST by a different org pharmacist -> old row soft-revoked, new row active (existing replace semantics under org access).

27. Org invitation full path (Phase 6 leftover): invitation minted with as_org + location -> intake meta returns organization_name + 'unverified' + location_label; walk to submitted; consent approve -> ACTIVE grant with organization_id + location_id; a different active member reads 200; consent deny -> zero grants of any kind and every member 403; replayed consent -> 409/410.
28. Org invitation staleness: walk to intake_submitted, deactivate the minter, patient POSTs consent -> 410, invitation 'cancelled' (audit meta reason 'minter_inactive'), zero grants created.

29. Reuse-scope regression (same-commit lookup fix): (a) a pending org care-code request for (P, org) is ACTIVATED IN PLACE by an org invitation consent — exactly one (P, org) grant row; (b) with a coexisting ACTIVE org grant for (P, clinician C's org), an INDIVIDUAL invitation from C concludes into a NEW/reused organization_id-IS-NULL grant and the org row is untouched.

30. Migration idempotency: build a DB containing the old ux_grants_open index and an open individual grant; run createDatabase twice -> no throw; ux_grants_open absent; ux_grants_open_individual, ux_grants_open_org, ux_org_members_single_active each present exactly once; the pre-existing grant untouched (organization_id NULL, status preserved) and still uniqueness-enforced.

31. Audit completeness + PHI-free sweep: full lifecycle (org_created, org_location_added, org_staff_invite_created/_redeemed or org_member_joined, access_requested meta.as='organization', access_approved, record_opened meta.org, access_revoked, org_member_role_changed, org_member_deactivated) all present in audit_events; org-admin events carry profile_id NULL (never surface in the patient feed); no meta value contains a name, email, or medication string — ids and enum strings only.

open_risks: Location is consent context, not an enforcement boundary: members are not location-assigned, so a patient approving 'Org — Main St' is visible to staff at every location. The consent copy says exactly that; true per-location scoping needs a member-location assignment table later (the most likely future rework — all three proposals and all judges agree).

Org grants deliberately survive membership churn: staff who join AFTER consent gain access without re-approval. This is the disclosed meaning of the grant, every open is audited with the actor's name, and revocation is one click — but patients may under-read the disclosure; the all-staff sentence carries real weight.

Anyone with a clinician account can create an org named like a real pharmacy; the ubiquitous 'Unverified organization' badge is the only defense until a verification process exists, and badge blindness is real. The care-code handover limits cold-approach abuse; org-scoped patient invitations carry the residual impersonation risk.

Staff-invite links are bearer tokens with no addressee: anyone holding an unexpired link with a clinician account can join. Mitigations: management-only minting, 7-day default/14-day max expiry, one-time redemption, minter-staleness cancellation, open_invite_count prompt at deactivation, rate limiting — residual risk accepted and documented in the README, matching the patient-invitation trust model.

The index split (ux_grants_open -> two partial indexes) changes a uniqueness invariant in flight: any code assuming at most one open grant per (profile, clinician) regardless of org — concretely the concludeIntake reuse lookup — silently mis-scopes if shipped separately. The db.ts and invitations.ts changes must land in the same commit; tests 29-30 pin it.

The alert-reviews org check is the one org authorization decision outside resolveProfileAccess; future write-ish endpoints (Phase 10 pharmacist dispositions) must replicate the membership + canReview pattern or reintroduce the fail-open. Mitigated by the CLAUDE.md hard-rule note and tests 25-26, but it remains a second enforcement point to remember.

One-active-org-per-user excludes locum/multi-banner pharmacists from org membership; they fall back to individual grants, fragmenting a pharmacy's roster view. Reversal is cheap at the schema (drop one index) but the singleton /api/org route posture would need :id variants — the route surface, not the data, is the real lock-in.

Blast radius: one compromised staff account now reads the whole org roster (view-only PHI). Compensating controls are per-request membership checks, instant deactivation, and per-open audit attribution; MFA remains on the known deferred list.
Roster cost: recomputeAlerts runs per patient per roster load and org rosters aggregate every consented patient; fine at pilot/SQLite scale, first thing to profile past a few hundred patients.

Org-admin audit events (org_created, member/invite lifecycle) are recorded with profile_id NULL but surfaced to no one in this phase — an owner-facing org activity view is deferred, so accountability exists in the table before it exists in the UI.

Sole-owner account loss still orphans org administration (members keep working; nobody can invite/deactivate/promote): succession exists only while an owner can sign in. Documented manual-DB-edit recovery in the README until an ops flow exists.

Patient comprehension of the two-door model is mitigated (overlap notes on both cards, post-revoke reminder) but unvalidated with real users; if pilot feedback shows confusion, the next step is a combined 'everything <person> can see' view rather than more copy.
